title: Key Priorities for ASEAN's Relations with US
what_it_is: Key Priorities for ASEAN's Relations with US

sections.label: US ties with ASEAN
sections.summary: The Minister says the short answer is economics: trade, investment and energy, with the US a critical partner for Singapore and ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan): Mr Speaker, the short answer to Mr Neil Parekh's question is economics – trade, investment, energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The United States (US) remains a critical partner for Singapore and for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The US is, by a significant margin, the largest foreign investor in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: And the US is also ASEAN's second largest trading partner.

sections.label: ASEAN and US economic benefit
sections.summary: The engagement benefits ASEAN and America, with ASEAN the world's fifth largest economy and US trade supporting jobs in both regions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: This engagement will continue to contribute in fact for mutual benefit of both ASEAN and America, and create an area in this part of the world which is safer, stronger and more prosperous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: It is worth reminding this House that in fact if you add, cumulatively, all the economies of the members of ASEAN, we already constitute the world's fifth largest economy and we expect to be on track to become the fourth largest economy by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The trade and investments from the US into our region support hundreds and thousands of jobs in Southeast Asia but similarly, it also supports over 600,000 jobs in America itself.

sections.label: Southeast Asia shipping lanes
sections.summary: One-third of global trade passes through Southeast Asia's maritime shipping lanes, including the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, and into the South China Sea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: Another point worth emphasising is that one-third of global trade passes through the critical maritime shipping lanes in Southeast Asia, including the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, and beyond that, into the South China Sea.

sections.label: Call with Marco Rubio
sections.summary: The Minister says the short answer is no and that he had an introductory telephone conversation with Secretary of State Marco Rubio the previous night.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And that is why I began my answer to you just now that the short answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And if I may add, I had I had an introductory telephone conversation with the Secretary of State Mr Marco Rubio last night.
